rows.selection_reason: With no prior experiments, the primary uncertainty is establishing a performance baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest, most interpretable configuration: it uses a standard linear encoder (PCA), the simplest profile setting, and a single modality. This gives a clean reference for RNA-alone performance against which all other design choices (image modality, multiprofile aggregation, learned encoders, multimodal fusion) can be measured. Starting here reduces the risk of conflating multiple variables and anchors the search so that subsequent experiments can isolate the contribution of each design dimension (encoder quality, profile aggregation, image modality, fusion strategy) within the tight 10-experiment budget.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved only ~48.5% accuracy, a weak baseline. The most critical uncertainty at this stage is whether the image modality is more informative than RNA for this task, since all remaining experiments (multimodal fusion, better encoders) depend on knowing which modality carries signal. Question: Does image-only (resnet50, singleprofile) outperform or underperform the RNA-only baseline? This is the cleanest modality comparison—same profile setting (singleprofile), no confounding aggregation or fusion—so any accuracy difference isolates the modality effect. Why this is the best next experiment: With 8 experiments left, establishing whether image features are competitive or superior to RNA features will determine whether to invest remaining budget in multimodal fusion configs or in improving single-modality representations (better encoders, multiprofile). Testing a multimodal config now would confound modality contribution with fusion strategy, making it harder to interpret results.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA n2000 (config_001) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while image-only with ResNet50 (config_010) is very weak at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. The key uncertainty is whether the PCA linear projection is the bottleneck for RNA representation. This experiment (config_004) tests scvi_n200 in an otherwise identical single-profile, RNA-only setup, isolating the effect of a learned nonlinear encoder vs. PCA. If scvi improves meaningfully over PCA, it justifies investing remaining budget in scvi-based multimodal or multiprofile configurations. If it does not, the bottleneck lies elsewhere (e.g., multiprofile aggregation or task difficulty), redirecting exploration. This is the highest-information single-variable comparison available and the best use of experiment 3 of 10.

Evidence: scvi_n200 singleprofile (0.5203) is the best configuration so far, outperforming pca_n2000 singleprofile (0.4849) and image-only resnet50 (0.2079). The largest untested design dimension is multiprofile vs. singleprofile — we have no data on whether aggregating multiple profiles improves accuracy. Question: Does multiprofile with avgpool aggregation improve upon the best singleprofile RNA result? This is a single-variable change from config_004 (adding multiprofile + avgpool), isolating the profile/aggregation effect on the strongest encoder. Why this is the best next experiment: With 6 experiments remaining, resolving whether multiprofile helps at all is critical — if it does, we can invest remaining budget in transformer aggregation and multimodal extensions; if it does not, we avoid wasting experiments on multiprofile variants and pivot to scgpt or multimodal testing. avgpool is the simplest aggregation, making this a clean, interpretable test before trying the more complex transformer.

The strongest evidence so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy, a large jump from its singleprofile counterpart (0.520). This isolates the multiprofile+aggregation effect as the most impactful design choice. The natural next question is whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool for the same encoder/profile setting. config_006 changes only the aggregation method (avgpool → transformer) while keeping rna_only, multiprofile, and scvi_n200 fixed, giving a clean single-variable comparison. This is the best use of the next slot because it directly exploits the strongest signal, tests a high-impact design axis (aggregation), and will inform whether to invest remaining budget in transformer-based pipelines or stick with simpler pooling before exploring multimodal fusion.

Evidence: Multiprofile + scvi_n200 is the strongest configuration so far (0.653 acc), with aggregation choice (avgpool vs transformer) showing negligible difference (~0.3%). Image-only models are very weak (0.21), suggesting the RNA signal dominates. Uncertainty: We have not tested whether a pretrained RNA foundation model (scgpt) can outperform the variational encoder (scvi_n200) in the multiprofile setting. This experiment isolates the RNA encoder effect while holding profile setting (multiprofile) and aggregation (transformer, matching the best result) constant. Rationale: If scgpt substantially beats scvi_n200, it reshapes the entire multimodal strategy for the remaining 4 experiments by providing a stronger base for fusion. If it is comparable, we confirm scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder and can pivot to testing multimodal fusion (e.g., scvi_n200 + ViT-L) in the remaining budget. This is a clean single-variable comparison that reduces uncertainty about the most important remaining design choice before committing to multimodal experiments.

The current best is config_006 (RNA-only, scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) at 0.653 acc. The key remaining question is whether adding the image modality to this best RNA setup can push accuracy higher. Image alone is weak (resnet50: 0.208), but it may carry complementary spatial/morphological information. Config_032 tests multimodal fusion (concat) with the exact best RNA configuration (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) plus resnet50, isolating the effect of adding image. This is the highest-value experiment because: (1) it directly tests whether multimodal can beat the 0.653 ceiling, (2) if it helps, the remaining 2 experiments can explore ViT-L or weighted fusion to push further, and (3) if it doesn't help, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and can spend remaining budget on minor RNA-side refinements. Concat is chosen over weighted as the simpler, more standard baseline fusion to first establish whether image adds any signal.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI_n200, ResNet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688 accuracy. The strongest evidence shows that scVI_n200 + multiprofile + transformer aggregation is the optimal RNA backbone, and adding ResNet50 image features with concat fusion improved over RNA-only by ~3.5%. The key uncertainty is whether the fusion strategy can be further optimized: weighted fusion allows the model to learn modality-specific importance weights rather than treating both branches equally via concatenation. Config_033 changes only the fusion method (concat → weighted) while holding all other settings identical to config_032, making it a clean single-variable ablation. With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, isolating the fusion effect is the highest-value exploitation step: if weighted fusion improves accuracy, it directly upgrades our best configuration; if not, we confirm concat is sufficient and can use the final experiments to explore the image encoder (ViT-L) as the remaining lever.

The current best is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.713 accuracy. The image-only resnet50 baseline was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image modality may be underperforming due to encoder capacity. Config_039 is a single-variable upgrade of the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other validated-optimal components (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion). This isolates the effect of image encoder quality on the multimodal pipeline. It is the most logical exploitation step: if a stronger image encoder contributes more signal in the multimodal setting, this could push accuracy above 0.713. If it does not, the remaining experiment can explore other directions. Testing this now (experiment 9) preserves one experiment for a potential follow-up or alternative if needed.

The current best (config_039, acc=0.7250) uses multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted. All component choices are well-supported by evidence: scvi_n200 >> pca_n2000 >> scgpt, imagenet_vit_l > resnet50, weighted > concat, multiprofile >> singleprofile. The only untested variation on this optimal stack is aggregation: avgpool vs. transformer. In RNA-only, these were nearly identical (0.6530 vs 0.6501), but in the multimodal setting with a strong ViT encoder, the interaction between aggregation and cross-modal fusion may differ. Config_037 (avgpool + weighted + imagenet_vit_l + scvi_n200 + multiprofile) isolates exactly this one change. As the final experiment, this is the highest-probability exploitation step: it keeps every other setting at its empirically validated optimum and tests the single remaining unexplored degree of freedom, giving the best chance of marginally exceeding 0.7250.
